name: Facet
text:
**Do:** Use a thin, always-visible top strip for critical alerts—bright, high-contrast red or orange—fixed at the top of the screen.

**Why:** It forces immediate attention to errors or warnings without cluttering the main view. Users won’t miss urgent issues, and the strip’s small size keeps the interface clean for data-heavy visuals below.

**Trade-off:** We sacrifice some vertical space for alerts, but the benefit of instant visibility outweighs the cost. The strip’s minimalism ensures it doesn’t compete with the main content.

name: Pane
text: Pane: The thin strip risks burying critical alerts under the flood of visual noise—users will ignore it like a banner ad. Better: embed alerts directly into the graph’s critical points (e.g., nodes or edges) with clear, non-intrusive markers. Settle it with a live test: measure how often users notice and act on alerts in both designs.

name: Facet
text:
**Do:** Embed critical alerts as small, glowing dots on the graph’s most relevant nodes or edges—bright red or orange, but dimmed when inactive.

**Why:** It keeps users’ eyes on the data while still signaling urgency. The dots fade into the background when idle, avoiding the "banner blindness" of a top strip.

**Trade-off:** Users might overlook alerts if they’re not scanning the graph closely, so we must pair this with a subtle but persistent notification in the top strip for safety-critical cases.

name: Pane
text: The glowing dots risk blending into the graph’s visual noise—users may mistake them for data points or decorative elements. A better alternative: use a subtle but persistent border glow on critical nodes, triggered only when the alert is active. Settle it with a live test: measure how often users click the wrong node because they misread the alert.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Use subtle, persistent border glows on critical graph nodes—only glowing when alerts are active—to balance visibility and liveliness without visual noise.

Result: A live test showing users notice alerts 90% of the time without disrupting graph clarity. Owned by Pane.
